page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g9it.24xlarge is an x86_64 instance from the Enhanced family built on the KVM hypervisor. It features 96 dedicated vCPUs powered by 3.2 GHz Intel Xeon 6982P-C processors, paired with 384.0 GB of system memory. This yields a standard balanced ratio of 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU, aligning it with general-purpose enterprise computing requirements.

The server does not include integrated local disk storage, requiring external cloud block storage for persistent filesystems. Network performance is supported by a 64 Gbps baseline bandwidth, providing substantial network throughput for multi-node clustering and distributed operations. No discrete GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses are provisioned with this instance profile.

From an operational perspective, the large dedicated core count and standard memory-to-vCPU ratio offer balanced density for scale-out workloads without paying a premium for memory-skewed or GPU-accelerated hardware. The lack of local NVMe storage means I/O-heavy applications depend entirely on attached storage configurations. Suitable workloads include large-scale web applications, enterprise ERP systems, microservices platforms, continuous integration pipelines, and distributed analytical tasks.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g9it.24xlarge is an Enhanced family general-purpose compute instance built on the KVM hypervisor and x86_64 architecture. Powered by dedicated Intel Xeon 6982P-C processors operating at 3.2 GHz, the server delivers 96 vCPUs alongside 384.0 GB of system memory, maintaining a 4.0 GB per vCPU allocation. The configuration contains no discrete GPUs and provides no onboard local storage, necessitating network-attached block volumes for system and runtime data. Network throughput is anchored by a high-capacity baseline bandwidth of 64 Gbps, facilitating rapid data transfers across distributed environments. Delivering substantial processing capability without the overhead of specialized hardware accelerators, the ecs.g9it.24xlarge is well tailored for enterprise application servers, large-scale container orchestration, continuous integration clusters, microservice frameworks, and distributed web serving deployments.
